title: Liability Already Taken Back on the Lines Outside Cover
content:
Money already taken back on the lines outside cover of a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is never taken back twice, and what has already come back is deducted from the liability restated.

*What is deducted where an entry already stands restating one of the lines outside cover?* The liability that entry has already taken back.

*What is deducted where no entry stands restating one of those lines, and an entry stands recording money recovered from the policyholder on one of them?* The amount that entry records.

*What is deducted where neither of those stands on the claim record?* Nothing already taken back.

### Points of judgement

The first question is settled first: where any entry already stands restating one of the lines outside cover, the liability it has taken back is the deduction, and entries recording money recovered from the policyholder do not come into it.

The second is reached only where no entry stands restating one of those lines. It then takes the amount recorded by an entry recording money recovered from the policyholder on one of them.

Where the claim record carries neither kind of entry against those lines, nothing already taken back is deducted.

### Hypothetical records

A claim record carrying a restatement of one of the lines outside cover that took back 62.00 of liability: the deduction is 62.00.

A claim record carrying no such restatement but an entry recording 45.50 recovered from the policyholder on one of those lines: the deduction is 45.50.

A claim record carrying neither: nothing is deducted.
